Workforce development: Create a formal talent pipeline for workers skilled in advanced energy technologies. Expand interdisciplinary training for information technology and operational technology professionals. Ensure workforce development plans cater to mission and technology- specific needs, such as deployability. Exercises and simulations: Expand black-start exercises to encompass more interdependent entities and longer outage durations. Expand use of exercises to account for compounding natural hazards and cyberthreats to create granular impact predictions and inform contingency planning. Investments in commercialized technology: Leverage proven technologies, including geothermal systems, hybrid tactical vehicles, solar plus storage, and microgrids, working with commercial providers to adapt them to defense energy needs. Operational testing and pilot programs: Broadly share lessons learned from pilot programs and prototype testing across services. Research into emerging technologies: Dedicate funding to encourage faster advancement of promising and potentially game-changing emerging technologies (e.g. optical/laser and radio frequency power beaming, quiet generator alternatives, and point-of-need fuel production). Partnerships and working groups: Establish partnerships and working groups to leverage domestic and foreign expertise on emerging technologies with military applications and to build capacity and improve interoperability in key regions, such as the Indo-Pacific. Common standards: Establish common energy technology standards (domestically and with partners) to promote interoperability, safety, and smoother adoption. Budget planning: Integrate the adoption of advanced energy systems into budget planning, using cost-saving approaches such as energy savings performance contracts (ESPCs). Repurposing infrastructure: Reuse legacy assets to reduce capital investment. Decommissioned missile silos and similar infrastructure can be converted into energy storage facilities using technologies such as gravity batteries, hydrogen, or compressed air, extending their utility and supporting distributed resilience goals. ix This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
